extracted.intended_audience: aspiring and practicing stand-up comedians, open-mic performers, MCs, and comedy students
extracted.subtask_description: A glossary-style how-to reference for stand-up comedy covering joke-writing, timing, stagecraft, heckler-handling, and MC duties. It gives definitions plus practical performance standards and anti-patterns used by comedians and teachers (e.g., Greg Dean's systems).

rubrics_metrics.name: Opening line
rubrics_metrics.description: First joke of stand-up comedy shows to get a laugh in the first fifteen seconds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performing technique used by comedians who design jokes specially to start routines and shows with a solid laugh; correlated with early LPMs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hurry a joke / Rush a joke
rubrics_metrics.description: Communicating a joke to an audience faster than they can comprehend the Setup's relationship to the Punchline, which can diminish or kill the laugh.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not deliver the punchline too quickly; allow processing time. See 'processing'—rushing is a common mistake that kills laughs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pause / take a beat
rubrics_metrics.description: When comedians stop talking after a punchline to allow time for the audience to laugh.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use silence to enhance tension or allow the audience to think; essential for comedy timing and avoiding step-on-laughs.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-liner timing
rubrics_metrics.description: After delivering a punchline, waiting for the laugh to peak, then pausing for the count of 2, 3, 4, then starting the next setup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific timing guidance for one-liners to avoid interrupting the laugh and to maximize LPMs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tag / tag timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional short punchline immediately following a punchline that does not require a new setup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use tags to extend laughs; place tags after the laugh peaks and maintain tag timing to keep momentum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step on laughs / talk over laughs / kill a laugh
rubrics_metrics.description: Speaking or taking actions after delivering a joke that causes audiences to not laugh or stop laughing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid continuing to speak after a punchline; this is an easy way to 'kill' the laugh. Take pauses instead of talking over laughter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stay in the bit
rubrics_metrics.description: After a Punchline during the audience laughter, stop talking and remain in the same emotion or state of mind as when the joke was delivered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staying in the bit gives the audience permission and space to laugh and keeps momentum for the next joke. Coined by Jerry Seinfeld.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laughs per minute (LPMs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measurement for counting the number of laughs in routines or shows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a performance metric (example: 'professional level of 5 laughs per minute'); abbreviated LPMs or LMPs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect the light / red light
rubrics_metrics.description: Signal(s) to comedians that their performing time is up (1-minute left / final and strongest signal to end).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When you get the light, respect it if you want to return to this club. Running the light can lead to MC intervention or being banned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smooth on and smooth off
rubrics_metrics.description: Best practices for getting on stage and off stage to ensure well run shows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manage stage entrances and exits professionally to maintain club relationships and show flow (phrase credited to Jerry Seinfeld).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mic technique
rubrics_metrics.description: Most effective ways of holding and moving the microphone, stand, and cord to enhance communication and smoothly get performers on and off stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical microphone handling is part of delivery; good technique supports clarity and stage movement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read on material
rubrics_metrics.description: When comedians perform their jokes and judge the audience's responses (laughter, groans, boos, silence, applause) to know how to adjust their script to get big consistent laughs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use audience feedback in real time to cut, expand, or alter bits; a central improvisational and iterative skill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor material
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpreting or altering material to fit a unique performing situation and different audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust references, examples, and emphasis based on audience makeup (e.g., cops in audience). 'Tailor' is an active technique to increase relevance and laughs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rehearsal Process (Greg Dean)
rubrics_metrics.description: Method of turning jokes or routines into scenes by acting them out using Narrator, Self, and Character POVs so comedians remember in pictures, sounds, and feelings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rehearse by acting scenes (not rote self-talk) to ensure natural recall and flexible performance. See companion books for thorough explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid improper rehearsal / talking head
rubrics_metrics.description: Improper rehearsal: practicing jokes by repeating only the words (self-talk), leading to memorized 'talking head' performances with no emotion or movement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improper rehearsal causes deliverers to rely on internal recitation and reduces performative flexibility; rehearse with acting and scene work instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joke structure (Greg Dean's model)
rubrics_metrics.description: Model demonstrates two sections of jokes, setup and punchline, linked by the five mechanisms: 1st Story, Target Assumption, Connector, Reinterpretation, and 2nd Story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the model to identify where a joke sits, fix weaknesses, and systematically write new jokes. Foundation for one-liners and storytelling structure differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setup
rubrics_metrics.description: First of two parts of one-liner jokes designed to misdirect the audience; establishes the Target Assumption or expected meaning of the Connector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarity in the setup is essential to create the Target Assumption; rewriting setups can make misdirection clearer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punchline / Reinterpretation / Reveal
rubrics_metrics.description: Second part of jokes that expresses the Reinterpretation or unexpected meaning of the Connector; the reveal is specific information often placed near or at the end of the punchline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the reveal near the end for maximum surprise; shorten punchlines where beneficial; punchline should shatter the Target Assumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target Assumption
rubrics_metrics.description: The expected interpretation of the Connector, established by the Setup to misdirect the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design the setup to build a strong, believable Target Assumption so the reinterpretation lands effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connector (one-thing-two-interpretations)
rubrics_metrics.description: The link between setup and punchline often expressed as '1 thing with 2 interpretations' that enables the reinterpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a connector that plausibly supports the Target Assumption but also allows a surprising reinterpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule of three / rhythm of three
rubrics_metrics.description: Joke format when a setup lists two positive items then the punchline reveals a third negative item that is compatible yet unexpected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the rhythm/rule-of-three structure to create patterns and violate expectation on the third item for comedic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sandwich / hammocking
rubrics_metrics.description: Technique of placing weaker material or improvisation between two strong jokes or routines (a metaphor: hammock between support beams).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use stronger jokes to support riskier or weaker bits; intersperse material to protect show flow and maintain audience engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heckler handling / heckler lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Prewritten, witty responses comedians prepare to use on different kinds of hecklers to get them to shut up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have a set of insult/comeback lines (heckler lines) memorized and appropriate to the venue; turning interruptions into comedy can enhance the show when handled skillfully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hurt line
rubrics_metrics.description: Subjective psychological tipping point when the pain within the comedy becomes real and turns mood into drama.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize the boundary between biting comedy and real hurt — a hurt line can silence a room; use caution as it can shift tone to drama.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set list / show list
rubrics_metrics.description: Bullet point reminders of the order of the jokes or routines to be done in a show.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a set list to manage pacing and transitions; helpful for remembering order during a performance and for tailoring flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage time
rubrics_metrics.description: The amount of time (duration in minutes) comedians get to perform at each specific show; also refers to the experience gained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acquire stage time to build craft; adapt material to slot length and respect timing constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crowd work / riffing
rubrics_metrics.description: Technique where comedians take an idea from an audience member's response and embellish it to discover humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Riffing turns spontaneous audience interactions into material; requires listening and quick improvisational skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scene work / storytelling structure (with POV shifts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stand-up storytelling that sets up scenes and acts them out using Narrator, Self, and Character POVs; storytelling requires acting, staging, tense control and scene work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Storytelling demands additional skills beyond one-liners (acting, staging); distribute setup/punch/tag among POVs and rehearse scenes to perform them naturally.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-liners (definition & delivery)
rubrics_metrics.description: Short jokes using a setup and a punchline; often contain two sentences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One-liners rely on tight setup/punch structure and precise timing; use one-liner timing and tags to maximize laughs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joke file / joke map / Joke Mine (writing system)
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep jokes collected and organized (joke file); Greg Dean's Joke Prospector System begins with a topic (Joke Map) then uses the Joke Mine to generate punchlines using the five mechanisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a joke file to organize material; follow structured writing systems (Joke Map -> Joke Mine) to systematically generate and refine jokes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punch up / punch down
rubrics_metrics.description: Punch up: make jokes about people/institutions with high status; Punch down: make jokes about those with lower status than the comedian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of the ethical and audience-impact differences between punching up and punching down; punching up is generally safer/more acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read the room / real audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinction between real customers and rooms full of comedians; performance strategies differ when the audience isn't a 'real audience.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize getting gigs in front of real audiences to test material honestly; strategies like tailoring and read-on are less meaningful if the crowd is mostly other comedians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect stage signals and club norms (get the light / run the light consequences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comedic professionalism includes acknowledging signals (lights) and club rules; running the light may lead to being forced off stage or banned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow venue cues and management requests; preserve future booking opportunities by being professional on timing and exits.
